title: The South China Sea throughflow as a heat and freshwater conveyor
query: Using the supplied CMOMS daily velocity, temperature and salinity for 2011-2020, test the following findings of Qu et al. (2006, Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2006GL028350): (1) the South China Sea throughflow, entering through the Luzon Strait and leaving through the other straits, is a conveyor that transfers up to about 0.2 PW of heat and about 0.1 Sv of freshwater from the South China Sea into the Indonesian maritime continent; (2) the surface heat and freshwater fluxes into the South China Sea vary differently in time from the throughflow; (3) the South China Sea acts as a heat capacitor, storing heat in some years and releasing it in others. Quantify the strait transports and the heat and freshwater they carry, state the reference temperature and salinity you use, and give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence. If a strait lies outside the supplied model domain, say so and adapt.

paper.title: South China Sea throughflow: A heat and freshwater conveyor
